question: On what basis is the determination of the level of a component of Human Development Index (HDI) made? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options: Gross National Income
Net National Product
Gross National Product
Gross Domestic Product
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gross National Income

Explanation:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is based on three main components: health, education, and standard of living. For assessing the standard of living, Gross National Income (GNI) per capita is used, not Gross Domestic Product (GDP). GNI reflects the total income earned by a country's citizens, whether within the country or abroad, providing a more accurate measure of living standards. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes HDI and incorporates GNI per capita in logarithmic form. Other options like GDP, GNP, or NNP are not used for this component. Thus, the determination of the level of this HDI component is based on GNI per capita.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Measure of living standard in HDI → GNI per capita
☛ Organization publishing HDI → UNDP
☛ Three components of HDI → Health, Education, Standard of Living
☛ Measure of health → Life expectancy at birth
☛ Measure of education → Expected years of schooling and Mean years of schooling
question_hi: मानव विकास सूचकांक (एचडीआई) के किसी घटक के स्तर का निर्धारण किस आधार पर किया जाता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019))
options_hi: सकल राष्ट्रीय आय
कुल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद
सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद
सकल घरेलू उत्पाद
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सकल राष्ट्रीय आय

Explanation:
मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) तीन मुख्य घटकों पर आधारित है: स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा, और जीवन स्तर। इनमें से जीवन स्तर के आकलन के लिए सकल राष्ट्रीय आय (GNI) प्रति व्यक्ति का उपयोग किया जाता है, न कि सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) का। GNI किसी देश के नागरिकों द्वारा अर्जित कुल आय को दर्शाता है, चाहे वह देश के अंदर हो या बाहर। यह जीवन स्तर का अधिक सटीक माप है क्योंकि इसमें विदेशों से प्राप्त आय भी शामिल होती है। संयुक्त राष्ट्र विकास कार्यक्रम (UNDP) द्वारा प्रकाशित HDI में GNI प्रति व्यक्ति को लॉगरिदमिक रूप में शामिल किया जाता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे GDP, GNP, या NNP का उपयोग HDI के इस घटक के लिए नहीं किया जाता।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ HDI के तीन घटक → स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा, जीवन स्तर

☛ शिक्षा का मापक → विद्यालयी शिक्षा के अपेक्षित वर्ष और औसत वर्ष

question: According to the 2011 census, which Union territory had highest sex ratio? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Chandigarh
Diu and Daman
Delhi
Puducherry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Puducherry

Explanation:
According to the 2011 census, among the Union territories of India, the highest sex ratio was recorded in Puducherry at 1037 females per 1000 males. This is significantly higher than the national average of 943. The high sex ratio in Puducherry is attributed to its high literacy rate and better healthcare facilities for women. In comparison, other Union territories had lower sex ratios: Chandigarh had 818, Delhi had 868, and Daman and Diu had 618. Puducherry's sex ratio was second only to Kerala among all states and UTs.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ State with lowest sex ratio in 2011? → Haryana (879)
☛ National sex ratio in 2011? → 943
☛ Which UT had the lowest sex ratio in 2011? → Daman and Diu (618)
☛ Literacy rate of Puducherry in 2011? → 86.55%

question: Companies that establish their production units in SEZs (Special Economic Zones), are exempt from tax payment for the time of initial ________. (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: One year
Six months
Three years
Five years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Five years

Explanation:
Under the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 in India, production units established in SEZs are entitled to significant tax exemptions. Specifically, these units receive a 100% tax exemption on income tax for an initial period of five years. This is followed by a 50% exemption for the next five years, and additional benefits for subsequent years. This incentive aims to boost exports, attract foreign investment, and create employment. The SEZ Act replaced the earlier Export Processing Zone (EPZ) model and came into effect in 2005. The policy is governed by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Initial tax exemption period in SEZ → 5 years
☛ When was SEZ Act enacted? → 2005
☛ Full form of SEZ → Special Economic Zone
☛ Objective of SEZ → Export promotion, attract FDI
☛ After full exemption, next benefit → 5 years at 50%
question_hi: जो कंपनियाँ एसईजेड (विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र) में अपनी उत्पादन इकाइयाँ स्थापित करती हैं, उन्हें प्रारंभिक _________ समय के लिए कर भुगतान से छूट दी जाती है। (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)

छह महीने
तीन साल
पांच साल

Solution: सही उत्तर है पांच साल

Explanation:
भारत में विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र (SEZ) अधिनियम, 2005 के तहत, SEZ में स्थापित उत्पादन इकाइयों को महत्वपूर्ण कर छूट प्रदान की जाती है। विशेष रूप से, इन इकाइयों को प्रारंभिक पांच वर्षों के लिए आयकर से पूर्ण छूट मिलती है। इसके बाद, अगले पांच वर्षों के लिए 50% छूट और उसके बाद पांच वर्षों के लिए अतिरिक्त छूट का प्रावधान है। यह प्रोत्साहन निर्यात को बढ़ावा देने, विदेशी निवेश आकर्षित करने और रोजगार सृजन के उद्देश्य से दिया जाता है। SEZ अधिनियम 2005 में 2005 में लागू हुआ, जो पहले के निर्यात प्रसंस्करण क्षेत्र (EPZ) मॉडल को प्रतिस्थापित करता है।

question: Which logo is related to the authentication of its quality standards on a product? (RPF Constable 2018 (14/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Ornate Nomination
Examined as OK
ISI (Indian Institute of Standards)
Make in India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is ISI (Indian Institute of Standards)

Explanation:
ISI mark is recognized in India for certification of quality standards of a product. It is issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), ensuring reliability for consumers. The ISI mark is commonly found on electrical appliances, cement, edible oils, and other industrial products. This certification indicates that the product meets specified standards. It has been in use in India since 1955, and consumers trust it for quality assurance.

☛ Who issues the ISI mark? → Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)

ISI (भारतीय मानक संस्थान)
मेक इन इंडिया

question: Which of the following certification helps consumers to get the assured quality of goods? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019))
options: Certificate issued by municipality or corporation
Agmark
Certificate issued by Sanitary Inspector
Certificate of Police Inspector
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agmark

Explanation:
Agmark is a certification mark issued in India to ensure the quality of agricultural products. It is regulated under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and applies to products like grains, spices, fruits, vegetables, oils, etc. Agmark assures consumers about the quality standards, including purity, freshness, and conformity to specified parameters. Its aim is to prevent adulteration in agricultural produce and guarantee quality to consumers. Agmark certification is also mandatory for exporting agricultural products. Other options like Municipality Certificate or Sanitary Inspector Certificate do not ensure the quality of goods in the same manner.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Agmark is related to which field? → Quality certification of agricultural products
☛ Agmark is issued by which authority? → Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
☛ Which products come under Agmark? → Grains, spices, fruits, vegetables, oils, etc.
☛ What is the main objective of Agmark? → Prevent adulteration and ensure quality
☛ Agmark certification is mandatory for which purpose? → Export of agricultural products
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा प्रमाणन उपभोक्ताओं को वस्तुओं की सुनिश्चित गुणवत्ता प्राप्त करने में मदद करता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019))

Explanation:
एगमार्क भारत में कृषि उपजों की गुणवत्ता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जारी किया जाने वाला प्रमाणन है। यह भारतीय खाद्य सुरक्षा एवं मानक प्राधिकरण (FSSAI) के तहत आता है और कृषि उत्पादों जैसे अनाज, मसाले, फल, सब्जियां, तेल आदि पर लागू होता है। एगमार्क उपभोक्ताओं को गुणवत्ता के मानकों का आश्वासन देता है और उत्पादों की शुद्धता, ताजगी और निर्धारित मानकों को प्रमाणित करता है। इसका उद्देश्य कृषि उपजों में मिलावट को रोकना और उपभोक्ताओं को गुणवत्ता सुनिश्चित करना है। एगमार्क प्रमाणन कृषि उत्पादों के निर्यात के लिए भी आवश्यक होता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे नगर निगम प्रमाण पत्र या स्वच्छता निरीक्षक प्रमाण पत्र वस्तुओं की गुणवत्ता सुनिश्चित नहीं करते।

question: The resources which get depleted after being used for years are called- (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Non-renewable resources
Renewable Resources
Non-natural resources
All of the above
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-renewable resources

Explanation:
Resources that are available in limited quantities and get depleted after years of use are called non-renewable resources. These resources cannot be replenished quickly by natural processes. Examples: coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear fuels. They take millions of years to form. Option 2 'Renewable resources' are those that can be used repeatedly, like solar energy. Option 3 'Non-natural resources' are man-made. Hence, the correct answer is non-renewable resources.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Fastest depleting resource → Petroleum
☛ Example of renewable resource → Solar energy
☛ Formation time of non-renewable resources → Millions of years
☛ State with largest coal reserves in India → Jharkhand
☛ Petroleum is also known as → Black gold

question: Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) is an example of- (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Private Sector
Public Sector
Central Public Sector Enterprise
None of these
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Private Sector

Explanation:
Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) was established in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata. It is part of the Tata Group, a private sector conglomerate. In India, industries are broadly classified into two sectors: Public Sector and Private Sector. Private sector enterprises are owned and managed by private individuals or groups. TISCO is entirely operated with private investment and management, making it an example of the private sector. In contrast, public sector undertakings are owned by the government. Since TISCO is free from government control, it clearly belongs to the private sector.

☛ Definition of private sector → Ownership by private individuals/groups
☛ Example of public sector → SAIL

question: What is included in the definition of minimum wages -  (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Bread, Textiles and Houses
Employment and Investment
Marriage and Employment
Cars, Employment and Aubrey
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bread, Textiles and Houses

Explanation:
Minimum wage refers to the lowest remuneration that an employer must legally pay to an employee. The definition of minimum wages typically includes the basic needs of bread (food), textiles (clothing), and houses (shelter). According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), minimum wage is the minimum amount that is sufficient to meet the basic needs of a worker and his/her family. In India, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 ensures that workers receive adequate wages for their livelihood. This act recognizes food, clothing, and housing as fundamental necessities. Other options like cars, investments, or employment-related aspects are not part of the definition of minimum wages, as it focuses on essential survival needs rather than luxury or secondary items.

question_hi: न्यूनतम वेतन की परिभाषा में क्या सम्मिलित है - (RPF Constable 2018 (16/02/2019) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following organizations is related to non-agricultural product market access (NAMA)? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))

solution:

question: The reduction of depreciation on the capital goods of a country is called the calculation of ____________. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)

Total national income
Net domestic product
solution:

Explanation:
When depreciation on capital goods is subtracted from a country's gross domestic product, we get Net Domestic Product (NDP). Depreciation accounts for the wear and tear or obsolescence of capital assets. NDP provides a more accurate measure of a country's economic output because it accounts for capital consumption. question: A declining exchange rate that reduces the value of one country's currency in comparison to other countries' currencies is called __________. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Depression
Inflation
Appraisal
Reverse Exchange
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Depression

Explanation:
A declining exchange rate that reduces the value of a country's currency compared to other currencies is called Depreciation. Currency depreciation occurs when the value of a currency falls in the foreign exchange market due to market forces (supply and demand), not government policy. Inflation is a rise in the general price level, Appraisal is an assessment of asset value, and Reverse Exchange is not a standard term. Thus, the correct option is Depreciation. Note that the given option "Depression" is likely a translation error; the standard term is "Depreciation."

question: Which of these is a system used in Indian economy? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Public Areas
Capital Economy
Private Sector
Mixed Economy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mixed Economy

Explanation:
The Indian economy is a Mixed Economy, where both public and private sectors play significant roles. The foundation of this system was laid by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1950, which envisioned a blend of socialism and capitalism. In a mixed economy, the government controls strategic industries like railways, defense, and energy, while the private sector is encouraged in consumer goods and services. This system aims to balance economic growth with social welfare. The Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) historically guided this approach. Economic reforms of 1991 increased privatization and liberalization, but the mixed economy structure remains intact, allowing both state intervention and market forces to coexist.

question: What is the market that is too much to buy from very few sellers?   (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Minority Dominance

Monopoly

solution:

Explanation:
A monopoly market is one where there is only one seller or very few sellers who control the market. In such a situation, buyers have limited choices, and the seller has significant power in price setting. This market structure is opposite to perfect competition. Monopolies have barriers to entry, such as high capital requirements or government licenses. The seller can control the price and supply of goods. Consumers have no alternatives, leading to higher profits for the seller.

question: Government of India buys foodgrains through __________.  (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Indian Food Corporation
National Agricultural Market
Ministry of Agriculture
Right brother's shop
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian Food Corporation

Explanation:
The Food Corporation of India (FCI) is the main agency of the Government of India responsible for the procurement, storage, and distribution of foodgrains. It was established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964. FCI procures wheat, rice, and other grains from farmers at the Minimum Support Price (MSP). question: When was the new system of joint indirect taxes called GST implemented by the Indian Govt. ? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/02/2019))
options: 2016
2018
2017
2015
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2017

Explanation:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India on 1 July 2017. This tax system unified various indirect taxes levied by the central and state governments. GST follows a dual structure comprising Central GST (CGST) and State GST (SGST). Prior to its launch, the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act 2016 paved the way for GST. The GST Council was established to decide on tax rates and rules. This reform was a historic shift in India's economy, aiming to implement the concept of One Nation, One Tax. It replaced multiple taxes like VAT, service tax, and excise duty, simplifying the indirect tax regime and promoting ease of doing business.

question: What is the sale or purchase of secondary government securities through auction by the Reserve Bank of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/02/2019))
options: Open Market Operations
Cash Reserve Operation
Second Operation
Repo auction
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Open Market Operations

Explanation:
The sale or purchase of secondary government securities through auction by the Reserve Bank of India is called Open Market Operations (OMOs). It is a key instrument of monetary policy used by RBI to regulate liquidity in the banking system. When RBI buys government securities, liquidity in the market increases, and when it sells, liquidity decreases. Cash Reserve Operation manages CRR, while Repo auction is for short-term borrowing. Second Operation is not a standard term.
